name: Petrobras 3W offshore oil-well sensor telemetry — predictive maintenance (production-choke pressure forecasting bundle)
citation: Petrobras. 3W Dataset 2.0.0 — real undesirable events in offshore oil wells. github.com/petrobras/3W. Vargas, R. E. V. et al., "A realistic and public dataset with rare undesirable real events in oil wells," Journal of Petroleum Science and Engineering 181 (2019) 106223.
description: 1-minute multivariate sensor telemetry from Petrobras 3W real offshore oil well WELL-00006 (dataset/1/WELL-00006_20170731170930.parquet) during an abrupt-BSW (basic sediment & water) failure event. Target `production_choke_upstream_pressure` is P-MON-CKP (production-choke upstream pressure, Pa); covariates are the other live channels — tubing pressure (P-TPT), annulus pressure (P-ANULAR), gas-lift downstream pressure (P-JUS-CKGL), and temperatures downstream-choke (T-JUS-CKP) and tubing (T-TPT) — supplied past-only (a sensor's future values are not known at forecast time). 1657 rows spanning 983 normal-operation minutes then the labeled failure; forecast frame is present=last normal minute, context 720 min, horizon 120 min into the failure. NON-EIA: Petrobras 3W is operator-released oilfield telemetry, independent of the U.S. EIA. Note: on this near-constant high-baseline signal, point accuracy is trivial and mis-calibrated (see the head-to-head) — normalise/detrend before forecasting.
preprocessing: 1. Downloaded the parquet instance dataset/1/WELL-00006_20170731170930.parquet from the Petrobras 3W GitHub repo (real offshore well, abrupt-BSW class-1 event, 1 Hz, 99,331 rows).

2. Kept only the live, non-frozen channels (P-MON-CKP, P-TPT, P-ANULAR, P-JUS-CKGL, T-JUS-CKP, T-TPT); dropped channels that were empty or single-valued for this well (e.g. P-PDG, QGL, ABER-*, ESTADO-*).
4. Recorded the failure onset (row 983, class transitions 0 -> 101 -> 1) for the eval frame; the class label column is excluded from the covariate panel (it is the target label, not an input).
5. Wrote the wide CSV: date, target_<P-MON-CKP>, then the 5 covariate channels.
6. No calendar/time-derived variables were present; the only notion of time is the shared timestamps list.

7. Renamed all variable names and units from snake_case codes to plain English (CSV row/column structure unchanged). Name and unit mapping — production_choke_upstream_pressure [Pa] -> "production choke upstream pressure" [pascals] (target; pressure upstream of the production choke (P-MON-CKP)); tubing_transducer_pressure [Pa] -> "tubing transducer pressure" [pascals] (covariate; downhole tubing pressure/temperature transducer pressure (P-TPT)); annulus_pressure [Pa] -> "annulus pressure" [pascals] (covariate; production-annulus pressure (P-ANULAR)); gaslift_choke_downstream_pressure [Pa] -> "gaslift choke downstream pressure" [pascals] (covariate; gas-lift choke downstream pressure (P-JUS-CKGL)); production_choke_downstream_temperature [°C] -> "production choke downstream temperature" [degrees Celsius] (covariate; temperature downstream of the production choke (T-JUS-CKP)); tubing_transducer_temperature [°C] -> "tubing transducer temperature" [degrees Celsius] (covariate; downhole tubing transducer temperature (T-TPT)).
